At the Sanctuary of Guadalupe in Mexico City, the architecture and the people are equally compelling. Pilgrims come to venerate the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe, around which an important part of the country's religious life has developed. A large square connects several church buildings, gradually revealing different periods of the complex's history.

The old basilica preserves traditional church architecture. Beside it stands the circular church, opened in 1976. Its green copper roof is easy to recognize from outside, while the spacious interior is arranged so that the image can be seen from different parts of the hall. A moving walkway in front of the altar allows pilgrims to approach it and continue moving.

A visit offers a glimpse of a living tradition that brings together people from different cities and countries. Spend some time in the square, compare the old and new churches, and observe what happens around you. The complex will interest travelers who want to understand Mexico better through its faith and art. Explore the sanctuary at an unhurried pace and remember that religious services take place here.

Colorful Belize City, the country's former capital, was founded by English settlers in the late 18th century at the mouth of Haulover Creek, where the Belize River enters the Caribbean Sea. The area was then an extensive marshland, transformed by human effort into the first major European city in the territory then known as British Honduras.

Belize City, on the Caribbean coast, is not only the largest city in Belize but also a major port and the country's former capital. Along its coastline are several remarkably picturesque lagoons, with reef islands offshore. Many tourists favor the local beaches for their white sand, exceptionally clean and clear water, and lack of currents.

Beyond the beaches, Belize City also offers opportunities to visit the ruins of Maya cities. In town, you can see the 19th-century St John's Cathedral, the oldest Anglican church in Central America; visit the Museum of Belize, housed in a former prison; explore the Maritime Museum with its interesting collection of artifacts and models; and visit the Coastal Zone Museum. The Museum of Belize, in the old prison building dating from 1857, contains an extensive collection devoted to the country's history and Maya civilization.

Belize City is Belize's largest transport, commercial, cultural and historical center, known for its architecture and history and still considered a symbol of the country. Along its colorful waterfront, lined with attractive two- and three-story buildings, the sea laps almost against the walls, and yachts bob in the mouth of Haulover Creek. From the city, you can set out for the magnificent reefs of Caye Caulker and Ambergris Caye.
